options.text: A compiled, statically typed, garbage-collected language
An interpreted, dynamically typed scripting language

questions.explanation: Go compiles ahead of time to a native binary, checks types at compile time, and reclaims memory automatically with a garbage collector.

questions.prompt: Which of these did Go's designers deliberately leave out? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Go has no exceptions (errors are return values), no class inheritance (it uses composition), and no manual free (it is garbage collected). Functions, of course, exist.

questions.prompt: The standard tool that formats all Go source into one canonical style is called ____.
questions.explanation: gofmt (invoked as `go fmt`) formats Go code the same way for everyone, ending debates about layout.

questions.prompt: Match each Go concept to its description.

pairs.right: A lightweight thread managed by the runtime
A typed conduit for passing values between goroutines
A directory of Go files compiled together

questions.explanation: Goroutines and channels are the built-in concurrency primitives; a package groups files; gofmt enforces one style.

questions.prompt: What marks a Go program as an executable you can run?
questions.explanation: An executable is the special `main` package with a `func main()` entry point; Go has no classes or annotations for this.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of running a program with `go run hello.go` in order.

items.text: Go compiles it to a native binary

questions.explanation: `go run` compiles the source to a temporary native binary and then executes it in one step — there is no separate interpret stage at runtime.
